hints: Look very carefully at the middle of each formula and spot which ones contain CH=CH and which ones contain only CH2 groups.
Remember saturated means every carbon-carbon bond in the tail is a single bond, so there are no C=C double bonds present.
walkthrough:
**Recall what saturated means**

Think of saturated as saturated with hydrogen. It means no carbon-carbon double bonds, only single bonds in the hydrocarbon tail.

Rule to spot it: look for C=C in the formula. If you see CH=CH, it is unsaturated.

**Sort the four fatty acids**

Caprylic acid is CH3(CH2)6COOH. Only single bonds, so saturated.

Lauric acid is CH3(CH2)10COOH. Only single bonds, so saturated.

Oleic acid has CH=CH in the middle, so unsaturated.

Palmitoleic acid has CH=CH in the middle, so unsaturated.

**Pick the saturated pair**

Only caprylic acid and lauric acid have no double bonds. That matches option A, so you can choose it with confidence.

options.A: Correct. Both caprylic acid and lauric acid contain only CH2 groups and no C=C double bond, so both are saturated.
options.B: Caprylic acid is saturated, but oleic acid contains CH=CH so it is monounsaturated, not saturated.
options.C: Lauric acid is saturated, but palmitoleic acid contains CH=CH so it is monounsaturated, not saturated.
options.D: Both oleic acid and palmitoleic acid contain a CH=CH double bond, so both are unsaturated.
